Write a Manifest to JSON

Source: R/lib_manifest.R
wrmnfjs.Rd

Writes a manifest to a JSON file, so the record of a run (its metadata, cross-checks and environment) can be kept next to the outputs, shared, and read back by any JSON reader. By default the file is pretty-printed for people; canonical = TRUE writes the byte-stable form that mnfdgst() hashes. The package's own JSON codec (tojs()) is used; jsonlite is not needed.

Usage

wrmnfjs(man, path, canon = FALSE)

Arguments

man

A manifest as returned by mkmnf() and built up with recrd().

path

Character scalar, the destination file path.

canon

Logical scalar, default FALSE. TRUE writes the canonical form instead of the pretty-printed one: one line, keys sorted, which is what mnfdgst() hashes. Use it when the file itself has to be byte-stable rather than read by a person.

Value

path (character scalar), invisibly.

Details

Numbers are written with 17 significant digits, so every double reads back exactly; NA and NULL are written as null, and length-one vectors as scalars. When the manifest's meta$synthetic is TRUE, or the session is flagged synthetic (see mkmnf()), meta$synthetic = true is written whatever the list says, so a file written from generated data always says so. An existing file at path is overwritten; the folder must exist.

Errors when path is not a single non-empty string, and (from base R) when the file cannot be opened for writing.

See also

mnfcanon(), wrsmrytxt().

Examples

man <- mkmnf(list(project = "demo"), env = FALSE)
man <- recrd(man, "rowcount", obs = 20, expd = 20)
#>   rowcount                                     observed = 20.0000      expected = 20.0000      [INFO]
path <- wrmnfjs(man, tempfile(fileext = ".json"))
file.exists(path)
#> [1] TRUE

# Round-trips back through the package's own codec.
back <- fromjs(path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
back$results$rowcount$status # "PASS" ("INFO" after synthetic data, see mkmnf())
#> [1] "INFO"

# the canonical form: one line whose SHA-256 is the manifest digest
cpath <- wrmnfjs(man, tempfile(fileext = ".json"), canon = TRUE)
identical(readLines(cpath), as.character(mnfcanon(man)))
#> [1] TRUE

# the path must be one string
try(wrmnfjs(man, c("a.json", "b.json")))
#> Error : `path` must be a single non-empty string
